visual_features: Medium-sized arboreal marsupial with distinctive spotted coat. Unlike all other Spilocuscus species, both males and females are whitish with black spots. Strong prehensile tail, hairless on underside for gripping branches. Amber or orange eyes with vertical slit pupils like cats or reptiles, enabling superior night vision. Long claws for grip on tree branches and grooming.
description: The Waigeou cuscus (or Waigeo spotted cuscus) is a species of marsupial in the family Phalangeridae, endemic to the small island of Waigeo in West Papua, Indonesia (part of the Raja Ampat archipelago). It is one of the least-studied cuscus species. Remains fairly common within its limited range, but its tiny geographic distribution makes it highly vulnerable to habitat loss, mining, and hunting. First described in 1822 by French zoologist Anselme Gaëtan Desmarest. Listed as Vulnerable on IUCN Red List with CITES Appendix II protection.
population_estimate: No precise population data available. Remains fairly common within its very limited range on Waigeo Island (approx. 3,155 km²) but highly vulnerable to habitat disturbance. Listed as Vulnerable on IUCN Red List.
habitat: Restricted to the small island of Waigeo off the northwest coast of West Papua, Indonesia (Raja Ampat archipelago). Inhabits primary and secondary tropical forests, spending most of its time in the tree canopy. Entire range is limited to this single island, making its existence extremely fragile.
threats: Palm oil deforestation - concessions sold on Waigeo Island encroaching on habitat
Mining concessions reducing available range on the small island
Hunting for meat and fur by local communities and outsiders
Extremely limited geographic range - any habitat reduction has disastrous consequences
No specific conservation protections currently in place
ecosystem_role: As an arboreal marsupial, the Waigeou cuscus plays a role in seed dispersal through its fruit-based diet, helping maintain forest diversity. Serves as prey for larger predators in the Raja Ampat ecosystem. Its presence indicates healthy, intact forest canopy on Waigeo Island. Contributes to forest regeneration through seed dispersal.
human_connection: The Waigeou cuscus is one of the 'forgotten animals' of West Papua - a cryptic species with little public awareness despite its vulnerability. Faces multiple threats from palm oil expansion and mining, industries with economic importance but devastating local biodiversity impacts. Has no formal conservation protections in place. Local communities hunt it for meat and fur. Its entire survival depends on protection of remaining forests of Waigeo Island.
